That is a story I just came up with!
Get yourself comfortable, little one! It's gonna be a little while!
Once upon a time, there was a little butterfly...
She was migrating to find more food.
However, in the middle of her flight for food, she was blown away by the wind!
She was lost in an unknown place with unknown animals...
First she met a strange red animal with black ears and a tail tipped white.
Despite his long, sharp teeth and amber eyes, he was kind.
Next the butterfly met an animal with a long, coiling body.
Despite her long, curved fangs and scary eyes, she was friendly.
Finally the butterfly met an animal with feathers and wide eyes.
Despite her sharp beak and tearing talons, she was welcoming.
Moral of the story: You can make friends everywhere you go.
One of my favorite stories!
One frosty morning, on the chilly tundras in the middle of winter, a young snow leopard thought he heard a sound.
He perked his rounded ears and curled his thick tail.
He listened closely, but no more sound rose above the horizon.
A while later, after the leopard had caught his prey and eaten, he heard it again.
His dilated eyes searched the mountains and his white whiskers twitched.
But once again, there was no more sound.
The pale leopard was on edge the rest of the day, ears always perked for the eerie song of the mountain.
He had fallen asleep and woken up the next time he hear it.
This time he hurried up to the tallest mountain he could find and look all around the frosty grasses.
He spotted faraway shapes, their head up and ears back.
The leopard had realized the sound was from giant dogs called wolves.
Moons, moons later, the leopard told the tale to his cubs.
But he left out the part of seeing the wolves. He wanted his cubs to have a wide imagination.
Moral of the story: Imagination knows no age.
